title: Large-deflection cantilever under a dead tip load against the elastica (solids)
source: The elastica of a cantilever under a vertical end load: K. E. Bisshopp, D. C. Drucker, Large deflection of cantilever beams, Quarterly of Applied Mathematics 3(3):272–275, 1945 (elliptic-integral solution); values computed by integrating θ″ = −(P/EI) cos θ by shooting (our own RK4, 20000 steps), agreeing with the table of K. Mattiasson, Numerical results from large deflection beam and frame problems analysed by means of elliptic integrals, IJNME 17(1):145–153, 1981, to all six digits

quantities.quantity: tip deflection δ_v/L at P L²/(E I) = 1
quantities.reason: hex20, 40 × 2 through the depth, L/h = 20: shear deformation (0.6 (h/L)² ≈ 0.15 % of the deflection) and the clamp's local restraint, both absent from the elastica

quantities.quantity: tip shortening δ_h/L at P L²/(E I) = 1
quantities.reason: as δ_v; the shortening is the smaller, second-order quantity, so its relative error is about twice the deflection's
